svg.text: 💡 Quick Botany Facts
• The pistil is the female reproductive organ (stigma + style + ovary).
• The stamen is the male organ (filament + anther).
• Petals attract pollinators; sepals protect the bud.
• The ovary matures into a fruit after fertilization.
• The receptacle is the thickened base of the flower.
• Pollen grains land on the sticky stigma to begin pollination.
🎮 Controls
🐝 Pollination & Reproduction
Pollen travels from anther (♂) to stigma (♀), enabling fertilization.
After fertilization, the ovary develops into a fruit containing seeds.
Pollinators: bees, butterflies, birds, wind, and water.

g.text: Remember the key distinction between male and female flower parts:
The stamen is made of two parts:
• Anther — the yellow sac that produces pollen
• Filament — the thin stalk holding the anther
Look for the thin stalks with yellow tips on the flower.
Tip: the anther is at the TOP, filament is BELOW.
The pistil has three sections top-to-bottom:
Look for the central flask-shaped structure.
• Petals — colorful, showy, attract pollinators (large pink structures).
• Sepals — small green leaves beneath petals (protect the bud).
• Receptacle — the swollen base where all parts attach (near the stem).
Sepals are OUTSIDE petals, receptacle is at the BOTTOM.
Review the correct placements below. Compare with your own answers!

Thickened base where flower parts attach
